Details
  • Paper: Deep High-Resolution Representation Learning for Human Pose Estimation, CVPR 2019, 2019-02-25
  • Original code: https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmpose at 5408bc76f5b8
  • Authors' code, not used: https://github.com/leoxiaobin/deep-high-resolution-net.pytorch (PyTorch): The mmpose port loads the model-zoo checkpoints retrained and evaluated in the OpenMMLab pipeline, with its own heatmap codec, instead of the authors' original scripts and weights.
  • Code licence: Apache-2.0 (permissive); files: LICENSE
  • Weights licence: Apache-2.0
  • Licence evidence: https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmpose/blob/5408bc76f5b848cf925a0d1857899011d8c5b497/README.md#license
  • Training data: COCO 2017 (train, instance annotations), ImageNet-1k (ILSVRC 2012 classification) (COCO 2017 keypoints; the HRNet backbone was initialised from ImageNet-1k classification weights)
  • Options: flip_test = False
  • Kernel libraries: cudnn_hacc, fvm_conv, fvm_extra, fvm_mb, fvm_r3
  • Variants: hrnet-w32, hrnet-w32-384, hrnet-w48, hrnet-w48-384
  • Outputs: keypoints, keypoint_scores, boxes, scores; label_set: coco-keypoints-17
  • Input size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32
  • Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): hrnet-w32 3000x4000 (0.5 GiB peak allocated, 0.5 reserved); hrnet-w32-384 3000x4000 (0.7 GiB peak allocated, 0.8 reserved); hrnet-w48 3000x4000 (0.5 GiB peak allocated, 0.6 reserved); hrnet-w48-384 3000x4000 (0.8 GiB peak allocated, 0.9 reserved)
  • hrnet-w32 1080x1920, first call: portable + torch.compile 21 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp16 26 s (ONNX + engine).
  • hrnet-w32-384 1080x1920, first call: portable + torch.compile 21 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp16 26 s (ONNX + engine).
  • hrnet-w48 1080x1920, first call: portable + torch.compile 21 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp16 27 s (ONNX + engine).
  • hrnet-w48-384 1080x1920, first call: portable + torch.compile 23 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp16 28 s (ONNX + engine).
  • hrnet-w32 original (fp32) 1080x1920: mmpose 1.3.2 inference_topdown (CPU cv2 crop, network, heatmap decode; flip_test off), all in the timed call
  • hrnet-w32 original 1080x1920: torch.autocast(float16) around the call; mmpose 1.3.2 inference_topdown (CPU cv2 crop, network, heatmap decode; flip_test off), all in the timed call
  • hrnet-w32-384 original (fp32) 1080x1920: mmpose 1.3.2 inference_topdown (CPU cv2 crop, network, heatmap decode; flip_test off), all in the timed call
  • hrnet-w32-384 original 1080x1920: torch.autocast(float16) around the call; mmpose 1.3.2 inference_topdown (CPU cv2 crop, network, heatmap decode; flip_test off), all in the timed call
  • hrnet-w48 original (fp32) 1080x1920: mmpose 1.3.2 inference_topdown (CPU cv2 crop, network, heatmap decode; flip_test off), all in the timed call
  • hrnet-w48 original 1080x1920: torch.autocast(float16) around the call; mmpose 1.3.2 inference_topdown (CPU cv2 crop, network, heatmap decode; flip_test off), all in the timed call
  • hrnet-w48-384 original (fp32) 1080x1920: mmpose 1.3.2 inference_topdown (CPU cv2 crop, network, heatmap decode; flip_test off), all in the timed call
  • hrnet-w48-384 original 1080x1920: torch.autocast(float16) around the call; mmpose 1.3.2 inference_topdown (CPU cv2 crop, network, heatmap decode; flip_test off), all in the timed call
  • hrnet-w32 load / first call: original 0.45 s / 0.383 s, portable 0.25 s / 0.564 s, kernels 2.53 s / 0.285 s
  • hrnet-w32-384 load / first call: original 0.42 s / 0.225 s, portable 0.25 s / 0.567 s, kernels 2.04 s / 0.254 s
  • hrnet-w48 load / first call: original 0.72 s / 0.225 s, portable 0.4 s / 0.34 s, kernels 2.1 s / 0.147 s
  • hrnet-w48-384 load / first call: original 0.53 s / 0.242 s, portable 0.39 s / 0.355 s, kernels 2.16 s / 0.212 s
  • Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

Measured

Top-down on the ground-truth person boxes (non-crowd, at least one labelled keypoint), no flip test; people ranked by the mean of their 17 keypoint scores (not mmpose's rescoring and OKS-NMS), so not the papers' AP; pycocotools OKS AP; whole-body models scored on their 17 body keypoints. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.
